draft.title: The February Revolution of 1917
card: In early 1917 Russia was in its third year of war against Germany. Huge army losses and a breakdown in food and fuel supplies in cities such as Petrograd caused anger.
In late February (by the Russian calendar of the time), strikes and protests spread across Petrograd. Many soldiers sent to restore order joined the crowds instead.
Without support from the army, Tsar Nicholas II abdicated in early March (by the Western calendar). This ended Romanov rule.

Two bodies then shared power. The Provisional Government, drawn from the old Duma (parliament), held official authority. The Petrograd Soviet, a council of workers and soldiers, held much practical influence over the soldiers and workers.
draft.remember: War and shortages brought down the Tsar, and power was then shared between two rival bodies.

a.q: Which event made the Tsar's fall certain in February 1917?
opts: Soldiers joined the protesters instead of stopping them
The Duma won a vote that removed him from office
German troops captured the city of Petrograd
The Petrograd Soviet declared itself the government
a.why: Once troops sided with the crowds, the Tsar had lost the force he needed to keep order, so he abdicated. The Soviet did not take over formally: official authority passed to the Provisional Government.
a.clue: Think about who the Tsar relied on to control crowds.

b.q: In March 1917 a factory worker in Petrograd says, 'The Provisional Government rules alone now.' Why is this inaccurate?
opts: The Petrograd Soviet shared power and had real influence
The Tsar had refused to abdicate and still ruled Russia
The Provisional Government had no official authority
The Petrograd Soviet had been banned by the Duma
b.why: After the abdication, the Provisional Government held official authority but the Petrograd Soviet shared power through its influence over workers and soldiers. The claim that the Government had no authority is wrong: it was the official government.
b.clue: Two bodies held power at once.

a.best: Soldiers joined the protesters instead of stopping them

b.best: The Petrograd Soviet shared power and had real influence

problems.detail: The date is wrong. Nicholas II abdicated on 2 March by the Russian (Julian) calendar, which was 15 March by the Western (Gregorian) calendar. 'Early March' is true only by the Russian calendar, so '(by the Western calendar)' should read '(by the Russian calendar)', or the Western date should be given as mid-March.
The clue 'Two bodies held power at once' all but restates the correct option, so it gives the answer away.

check.summary: The card gives the abdication as early March 'by the Western calendar', but it was 2 March by the Russian calendar and 15 March by the Western one. The clue for question b nearly states the answer.

problems.detail: The card says Nicholas II's abdication on 2 March 'ended Romanov rule'. Strictly, he abdicated in favour of his brother Grand Duke Michael, and Romanov rule ended only when Michael declined the throne on 3 March. Consider 'This soon ended Romanov rule' or a mention of Michael's refusal.
